stories.headline: Over 400,000 march across France; clashes in Paris
body: About 410,000 people marched across France on Saturday, the government said; unions said twice as many.
Most marches were peaceful, but police used tear gas and a water cannon in Paris, with clashes in Marseille, Lyon and other cities.
Protesters are angry about living costs, school funding and fuel prices, and nearly 1,000 people were detained.
stories.vc: Street pressure makes it harder for France to cut spending, which can push up its borrowing costs. European investors will watch French bonds closely.

stories.headline: Gunmen kill 7 at a church funeral in southern Jordan
body: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan's Karak region on Friday, killing seven people.
Dozens more were wounded, and officials called it a terrorist attack by extremists.
King Abdullah II vowed the harshest response, and Jordan declared three days of mourning.
stories.vc: Jordan is usually one of the region's calmer countries. Attacks like this raise risk costs for tourism and regional business.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine keep striking even as peace talks return
body: A big Russian attack on Ukraine's energy system cut power to more than 500,000 people, Ukraine's energy ministry said.
The strikes came less than a day after both sides signalled that US-brokered peace talks were moving forward.
Russia says it is ready to resume talks next month, and the two sides also swapped the bodies of fallen soldiers.
stories.vc: Grid attacks keep Europe's energy market tense. Repairs, grid equipment and backup power are where rebuilding money will flow.

stories.headline: China's Communist Party opens a key four-day meeting
body: China's ruling Communist Party opened its fifth plenum in Beijing on Monday, a closed-door meeting that runs until Thursday.
Xi Jinping presented a work report focused on tightening discipline inside the party.
Analysts see it as perhaps the last big party meeting before leadership changes in 2027.
stories.joke: Four days behind closed doors to talk about discipline. Sounds like every startup offsite.
stories.vc: Big China policy shifts often follow these meetings. Watch for signals on the private sector and tech, which matter for supply chains and Asian markets.

stories.headline: Pakistan reopens a key border crossing with Iran
body: Pakistan reopened the Gabd-Rimdan crossing with Iran on Saturday, ending a week-long halt to trade.
Trucks carrying LPG and food were stuck during the closure, which came as Pakistan faced record LPG prices.
Days earlier, gunmen set dozens of parked trucks on fire near the closed crossing.
stories.vc: Border shocks show how fragile regional supply lines are. For importers, a second route or supplier is cheap insurance.

stories.headline: MakeMyTrip swings back to profit
body: Travel booking company MakeMyTrip made a net profit of $1.8 million in July to September.
In the same quarter a year earlier, it lost $5.7 million.
Revenue rose only 2.5% to $235.2 million, so growth is slow even as it makes money.
stories.joke: Profit is back, growth is on leave. Even the holidays need a holiday.
stories.vc: Profitable but slow-growing tech firms get valued more like old-economy companies. The next leg needs new products, not just cost cuts.

stories.headline: Pune police ask Google and Apple to pull the Rapido app
body: Police in Pune asked Google and Apple to remove the Rapido app from their app stores.
It follows a police case against Rapido's parent company for running bike taxis without the needed licence and approvals.
The case names Roppen Transportation Services, the company behind Rapido.
stories.joke: Rapido's fastest ride yet: from the road straight to the app store exit.
stories.vc: Regulation is the biggest risk for mobility and gig startups in India. Check a company's licences state by state before investing.

stories.headline: Bengaluru–Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper train likely from Nov 1
body: A Vande Bharat sleeper train between Bengaluru and Mumbai is likely to start on 1 November.
It will run overnight with 16 coaches and stop in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.
India's first Vande Bharat sleeper train runs from Kamakhya station in Assam.
stories.joke: Bengaluru to Mumbai overnight: skip both cities' traffic in one ticket.
stories.vc: Faster overnight trains between business hubs cut travel costs for sales and supply teams. Rail upgrades also lift real estate near stations.

stories.headline: Bengaluru's bus drivers and street workers show weaker lungs
body: A study of more than 10,000 frontline workers in Bengaluru found reduced lung function.
BMTC bus drivers, traffic police, construction workers and pourakarmikas (city cleaners) were tested.
It links polluted air to weaker lungs, obesity and diabetes, with pourakarmikas the worst affected.
stories.vc: Air pollution is a health cost that hits workers and productivity. Clean-air tech, electric buses and worker health services are big openings.

stories.headline: Aerospace parts maker Aequs grows fast but loses more
body: Aequs, a maker of aerospace parts, grew its operating revenue about 45% in July to September.
But its net loss widened to ₹52.4 crore, from ₹20.6 crore a year earlier.
That is a loss about 2.5 times bigger than last year.
stories.joke: Revenue took off. Profits are still taxiing on the runway.
stories.vc: India's aerospace parts makers are growing with global plane demand. Watch for the point where scale turns losses into profit.

stories.headline: Imarticus Learning plans a ₹1,000 crore IPO
body: Edtech company Imarticus Learning plans to file for a ₹1,000 crore IPO, Inc42 reports.
It aims to file its papers with SEBI through the confidential route within the next two to three months.
stories.joke: An edtech IPO: finally an exam the founders have to pass.
stories.vc: Profitable upskilling firms are reopening the edtech IPO door after the crash. Watch the pricing for clues on how the sector is valued now.

stories.headline: Warhound raises $200M to engineer military dogs
body: Warhound, started by Colossal's Ben Lamm and Anduril's Palmer Luckey, raised $200 million at a $1.2 billion valuation.
It plans to genetically engineer dogs for the military, police and rescue teams; the dogs don't exist yet.
Investors include Sequoia, 8VC and In-Q-Tel, the venture firm backed by US intelligence agencies.
stories.joke: A $1.2 billion company whose product is still a puppy plan. Very good-boy valuation.
stories.vc: Defence tech now spans biology, not just drones and software. Big funds are backing founders with a track record in hard science.

stories.statLabel: parameters, built to run on Macs
stories.headline: Meta's new open AI model is built to run on Macs
body: Meta launched Muse Spark Open, which it calls the most capable open-weight AI model made in the US.
It has 816 billion parameters and was designed with Apple to run locally on linked Mac Studio computers.
Running AI on your own machines adds security and saves money, the companies say.
stories.joke: Meta and Apple teaming up. Your Mac now needs a bigger desk and a bigger budget.
stories.vc: Strong open models shrink the moat of paid AI APIs. Startups can build on them and keep data on their own hardware.

stories.headline: Unacademy's founders are raising a ₹700 crore fund
body: Unacademy cofounders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are raising ₹700 crore for a new fund, Longshot Capital.
It will back AI and deeptech startups.
stories.joke: From teaching exams to grading pitches: the ultimate career test.
stories.vc: Founder-run funds often see deals early through their networks. For founders, an operator investor can help more than a bigger cheque.

stories.headline: L Catterton invests in InMobi's Glance for a US push
body: Consumer investment firm L Catterton has made a strategic investment in Glance, an AI shopping platform backed by InMobi.
Glance will use it to grow its AI shopping business in the US.
stories.joke: Your lock screen wants to sell you things. Now in American English too.
stories.vc: Indian consumer-tech firms are taking AI products to the US for bigger wallets. A brand-focused investor like L Catterton can open retail doors there.

stories.headline: AI trading platform Tradl raises a $4.1M seed round
body: AI-powered trading platform Tradl raised $4.1 million in seed funding, Inc42 reports.
Nexus Venture Partners, Stellaris Venture Partners and a few angel investors put in the money.
stories.joke: An AI that trades. Let's hope it panics less than we do.
stories.vc: AI tools for retail traders are crowded, so trust and distribution matter most. Watch how they handle risk and regulation.
